items: Course home
Pick an exam, join the live class, switch between QA, LRDI and VARC, ask a doubt, and learn topic by topic. Name blurred.
Topic path
Each topic goes in order: videos before class, the live class, an application class, assignments and a practice session.
Concept + application classes
Each concept class is paired with an application class. The screen lists 120+ live classes and 150 application videos.
Application class
Students solve questions live during class and see how many others answered. Student names blurred.
Live classes
Past and upcoming classes, which you can filter by subject, topic and sub-topic. Names blurred.
Assignments
Practice modules by topic: 20 for LRDI, 40 for Quant and 14 for VARC. You can pick up where you left off.
Daily Target
A free test every day with a leaderboard and streaks. Student names blurred.
Quiz analysis
Your overall score, a percentile meter, your All India Rank and your percentile in each section.
Doubt solving
Teachers solve doubts 24×7. The screen says the average reply comes in under 8 minutes.
Doubt discussion
A student’s doubt with a photo of the book page and a reply in the thread. Student name blurred.
Community feed
The open CAT Preparation group, with discussions, doubts, news and featured live classes.
Speed Read
A tool to help you read faster for VARC. You choose the topic, speed, text size and number of words.

extra.title: iCAT mocks and analysis
items: Error Tracker
Sorts each wrong answer by reason, such as a silly mistake, running out of time or falling for a trap answer, and shows the pattern in a chart. Student name blurred.
Goal Tracker (iRadar)
A radar chart compares your scored and target percentile in each section, and lists the B-schools you could get into at that level.
Mock Comparison
Puts your mocks side by side, and compares them with a 99 percentile benchmark and the average of 100 percentilers.
AI mock analysis
An AI-written report after each mock that explains where you lost marks in each section and what to fix first.
AI Mentor
A chat helper next to your mock analysis. You can ask about your score, your weak areas or a study plan. Student name blurred.
Learning gap detection
Shows your learning gaps by how much they cost you, the root causes of your mistakes, and suggested next steps by topic.
iCAT mock screen
The test screen, with section tabs, a timer and a question panel. iQuanta says its mocks follow the latest CAT pattern and level.
Practice menu
Study Room by section, Daily Targets, Quant and Verbal Rush games, a Reflection Room and formula revision.
Study Room
Topic cards that show the difficulty level and how many questions and tests you have done.
Topic test
Timed tests of five questions, with buttons to report a problem, use a calculator or bookmark.
Free mock test
Full-length mock: VARC 24, LRDI 22 and Quant 22 questions, 40 minutes each.
Mock interface
Made to look like the real CAT screen, with a question panel and section tabs. Account name blurred.
Video library
Live classes, topic videos, PreCAT and revision videos, with your progress shown for each section.
Premium modules
You must join to unlock Quant Shortcuts and LRDI Basics. General Knowledge videos are coming soon.
Topic-wise learning
Notes, example sets, concept videos and concept tests for each topic.
Mock test library
PreSimCATs and SimCATs for 2026, each two hours long. Finished tests are marked, and you can revise them.
SimCAT test screen
Set out like the real CAT screen, with section tabs, a question panel and the marking scheme. Student name and ID removed.
Test summary
As soon as the test ends, you see how many questions you attempted, got right, got wrong and skipped in each section.
Scorecard
Your score and percentile in each section, a predicted CAT percentile, and analysis by topic and by question.
Percentile mapper
The section and overall scores you need for each percentile.
Solution review
Every question with your answer, an “Analyse with AI” button, filters and bookmarks.
Video solutions
Statistics, text and video solutions for each mock question. Faculty face blurred.
Create your own quiz
Build a quiz from past CAT questions or IMS practice questions, by topic, difficulty and number of questions.
Batches page
CAT batches with the offer prices shown in November 2026: MBA Core 2027 ₹9,499, MBA Pro 2027 ₹14,999, MBA OMETs 2026 ₹1,999. Name and faculty photos blurred.
Mock test screen
Section tabs, a question panel, an on-screen keypad for typed answers and the marking scheme. Name blurred.
Lecture library
Topic lectures with notes and DPPs (daily practice problems) as PDFs and videos. You also earn XP points for watching. Faculty photos blurred.
Video solutions
A video walkthrough for each mock question.
Result summary
After each mock you see your score, predicted rank and a leaderboard, and you can retry the test or view solutions.
Mock instructions
120-minute tests with an on-screen calculator and a CAT-style question panel. Name blurred.

minus: Tests and mocks harder than CAT
Mocks and practice sets are much harder than CAT. Some students found this discouraging early in their preparation, and one said the LRDI sets looked nothing like past papers.
Syllabus finishes late
One batch was told the syllabus would finish by September, but it ran late. Extra “Booster” classes were added close to the exam, so little time was left for practice.
Too deep for average students
The content goes deeper than CAT needs, so students with average basics felt lost. One said it suits students who are already strong.
Long classes, hard with a job
Live classes of 2.5 to 3 hours were hard to fit around work.
Gaps in CAT-style practice
Students must do past papers on their own, there is little practice at forming equations, and students called the VARC part weak.
Slow support
One student waited months for solutions to a question PDF they uploaded, and another felt their feedback was ignored.
Faculty changes
One student found it hard when teachers kept changing.
plus: Free YouTube lectures
Two students recommended the free YouTube playlist, but as a choice instead of the paid course.
Fun teaching style
One student found the teaching fun.
Suits strong students
One said it works for students who are already near the top.
shots: Comment, about 3 months old
Calls it maths coaching, not CAT coaching. Past papers are left to students, sets are harder than CAT, and support did not reply for months.
Comment, about 1 month old
An R6-batch student says the syllabus promised by September wasn’t finished, and “Booster” classes were added late.
Comment, about 2 months old
Says it suits students who are already strong. Topics are not finished on time, and mocks feel scary early on.
Post
A long review that mentions confusing depth, 2.5–3 hour classes, discouraging mocks, changing teachers and a slow syllabus.
Three replies, about 3 months old
Says it is hard to manage with a job, the content is confusing, and they felt lost even with good basics.

ti.when: posted between 2023 and 2026, 7 of them in the past year
minus: Teaching depends on the teacher
Several said only some teachers were good, usually in Quant. Others called the teachers weak or careless.
Old, unreliable website
A classroom student said the site has kept crashing since January, and a 99.5 percentiler called it very outdated.
VARC and DILR teaching weaker
Students called VARC too basic and general, and one found better DILR and VARC help on YouTube.
Less suited to beginners
One student told beginners not to join, and another felt teachers mostly help students who are already doing well.
Slow response to problems
Complaints are sent to an email address and nothing gets fixed. One student said teachers forgot sessions they had planned.
Mocks easier than recent CATs
A 99.5 percentiler found the QA and DILR mocks much easier than CAT 2025.
plus: AIMCAT mocks worth taking
Students recommend the mocks even when they don’t like the course. Two comments from about 3 years ago found them the closest to that year’s CAT.
Strong Quant teaching
Three students praised the Quant teaching, and two of them named one teacher.
Good material and questions
One said the material covers most types of past-paper questions, and the questions are good.
Interview preparation
One found the low-cost GDPI preparation, with 7–8 mock interviews, worth the money.

eg.when: posted over roughly the past two years
minus: Slow or no replies to students

Students say messages to teachers often go unanswered, especially after low marks, and that mentoring ignores average students. Doubt replies in the app can take more than a day and often just say to watch the recording. One found a reply rude.
Little structure or practice

Students found the course loosely planned. They mention too few practice questions per topic, repeated questions, practice PDFs held back, PYQs left to the end, and no tips on saving time or choosing questions.
Syllabus runs late, then piles up

In one batch that began in April, much of Quant, including Geometry, was still pending in late July. Students describe long catch-up sessions, an overloaded November, and being told to finish topics from recordings.
Weak VARC teaching
Four students were unhappy with VARC. One said it is hard to learn English when it is taught in Hindi, and another stopped going to VARC classes.
App and live-class glitches
Students describe buffering even on fast internet, videos that pause or close on their own, repeated Zoom log-ins and a live chat that is rarely open. One said the app team blamed their internet.
Would not recommend it
Three said they regret joining or would not recommend it.
Long, slow classes
Two found the classes long and slow to sit through, and one now mostly studies alone.
Old material, hard for non-engineers
One student found the material and videos old, and Geometry too hard to finish as a non-engineer. They also felt the XAT course was not worth the money.
plus: Good teaching
Three students praised the teaching even while criticising the course. One liked Hunny Malhotra’s classes, one said he works hard, and one said the way they teach is great.
shots: Five comments, less than a day old

In a batch that began in April, much of Quant was still not done by late July, practice PDFs were held back and the live chat was rarely open. Others say doubt replies take over a day, Geometry is still pending, and they stopped going to VARC classes.

pw.when: posted between about 7 months and 2 years ago
minus: Mocks and practice don’t match CAT

Students disagree on whether they are too easy or too hard, but agree they are not at CAT level. One scored about 40 in PW’s VARC sectionals but only about 22 in other coachings’ tests. Another found the full mocks far harder than past papers, with even the top scorer getting 40–60 out of 204. A third called the mocks the worst.
Would not recommend it
Three said they regret joining, would not recommend it, or told others not to choose it for the low price alone.
Some teachers only average
Students rated some teachers as average or slow. One found an RC teacher easily distracted by the live chat, and another did not like the DILR teachers’ attitude.
Slow or no support

One student paid extra for one-on-one mentoring, but the mentor never joined the session, and a support ticket got no answer for 3 weeks. Another said calls about the app or other problems go unanswered.
Classes cancelled, then a packed schedule
Many classes were cancelled when the batch began, then moved into 5–6 classes a week, which was hard to manage with a job.
Mistakes in DPP questions
One student kept finding DPP questions where the solution assumed something the question didn’t say.
Few students take the mocks
Far fewer students take PW mocks than CL or T.I.M.E. mocks, so your rank means less, and the top score shown may not be a topper’s.
OMET and interview prep not tailored
One said the OMET course uses the same kind of questions for every exam, with no separate plan for each, and called the GDPI preparation poor.
Slow book delivery
Printed books took about 3 weeks to arrive.
Doubts about online praise
One commenter believes Rahul Bathla is a good marketer who posts fake posts and comments to praise himself. This is their opinion, and we could not check it.
plus: Strong Quant teaching
Three students praised the Quant teachers. One managed 10 QA attempts at 90–100% accuracy just from Rahul Bathla’s free YouTube lessons on arithmetic and algebra.
Some other teachers liked
Students liked some VARC and DILR teachers too. One found the VA teacher’s tips very helpful, and another recommended the DILR teacher for beginners.
shots: Post, about 10 months old

An MBA Pro 2026 student says many classes were cancelled at the start, then packed into 5–6 a week. They liked both Quant teachers, found mistakes in DPP questions, and say the paid one-on-one mentor never joined. They would not recommend it.

minus: Teaching is weak or depends on your centre

One student called the teaching the worst if you really want to learn, and another said the teachers are not that great. A classroom student said your experience depends on the teachers at your centre.
Not worth the money
Three felt they did not get their money’s worth. Two paid ₹23,000 and ₹30,000, and one said free YouTube videos and practice papers online would do.
Less practice than expected

A student who joined the self-learning program found about 30 Quant questions per topic and fewer than 100 DILR sets, far less than they expected. They were told more would be added over time, which they say was not mentioned before they paid, and the fee was not refundable.
Weak explanations

One student found the VARC explanations hard to accept, which hurt their confidence. They said Quant solutions jump to the answer without showing how to get there, and questions were either very easy or very hard.
SimCAT percentile far below CAT
The same student kept scoring about 70 percentile in SimCATs, then spent the last month on past papers and got 96 in CAT.
No follow-up after you pay
One student got messages every day before paying, but now says no one checks on their progress or attendance, and their doubts go unanswered.
Sectionals not good
One student liked the full mocks but called the sectional tests bad.
plus: Mocks worth taking
Three students rate the mocks highly, even when they criticise the course. One suggested taking only the mocks and learning elsewhere.
Useful material and online resources
One called the study material top notch, and a classroom student found the online resources really useful.

cl.when: posted between a few days and about 1 year ago
minus: VA questions confusing and unlike CAT

Two students said their VARC scores drop in CL mocks. VA questions, especially para summaries, have options that are nearly the same. One student who scores 45+ in VARC in other mocks had not got a single VA question right in CL’s.
Wrong or confusing solutions
One student found several wrong questions and solutions in the test series, mostly in DILR, with explanations that made no sense and question wording that was hard to follow.
Poor DILR videos
One student called the DILR videos poor and cheaply made. They felt only Gejo sir’s VARC videos are made with care.
plus: QA, LRDI and RC at a good level

TAKE.res: Each institute counts results in its own way, so you can’t compare the big numbers directly. Many students join more than one institute, so the same topper can show up on several pages.
TAKE.fac: Six of the eight name their lead teachers and publish their percentiles, and most are 99.9 or above. Career Launcher and T.I.M.E. publish none.
TAKE.rec: A big library matters less than knowing what to watch and practise next. Cracku and iQuanta build their recordings into a guided path, while the others mostly give you a library to browse.
TAKE.pra: Cracku and iQuanta publish the biggest question banks, and Elites Grid publishes no count. But the numbers are not counted the same way. iQuanta’s covers all its products, while most others cover one course.
TAKE.dou: Most institutes now offer 24×7 doubt support, but only iQuanta says how fast it replies. All claims about speed and hours come from the institutes themselves.
TAKE.moc: Students still trust IMS and Career Launcher most for predicted percentiles. Cracku and T.I.M.E. mocks, and Rodha’s VARC section, are seen as harder than CAT.
TAKE.app: All eight have a website, and all except Career Launcher list a mobile app. The bigger differences are how well the app guides your study and how smoothly it runs.
TAKE.con: Most split their content into a basic stage and an advanced stage. iQuanta and Career Launcher also run starter courses for non-engineers. What differs most is how close the material is to CAT level.
TAKE.com: Telegram groups are the main way T.I.M.E., IMS and Career Launcher students talk to each other. iQuanta and Cracku have the widest student groups, while PW and Rodha list no student community.
TAKE.men: All eight offer some mentoring, but how much varies. IMS offers up to 7 one-on-one sessions, PW offers 5 and Career Launcher offers 4.
